proofs.proof_tex:
Assume that \(\mathrm{oeq:global\text{-}endpoint\text{-}response}\) is resolved affirmatively.  Fix the confidence level \(\delta=0.05\), which belongs to \((0,1/4)\).  By \(\mathrm{thm:uniform\text{-}margin\text{-}band}\), for every sufficiently large \(n_\ast\), the test \(\Psi_n\) then satisfies
\[
 \sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathcal M_s:\,\gamma_{pq}\le0}
 \mathbb P_{\mathbf P}(\Psi_n=1)\le0.05
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathcal M_s:\,\gamma_{pq}\ge3w_n}
 \mathbb P_{\mathbf P}(\Psi_n=0)\le0.05<0.20.
\]
Thus \(\Psi_n\) is feasible in the optimization defining \(\rho_n^\ast\) in \(\mathrm{def:testing\text{-}frontier}\) at separation \(3w_n\).  By the defining infimum,
\[
 \rho_n^\ast\le3w_n
 =3\left(\frac2m+\frac{2M}{m^2}\right)C_1
 \left\{\frac{\log(C_0Rn_\ast/0.05)}{n_\ast}\right\}^{s/(2s+d)}.
 \tag{1}
\]
Put \(A=C_0R/0.05>0\).  For \(n_\ast\ge\max\{2,A\}\),
\[
 \log(An_\ast)=\log A+\log n_\ast
 \le 2\log n_\ast.
\]
Because \(s/(2s+d)>0\), equation (1), with all fixed factors absorbed into a finite constant \(C\), gives
\[
 \rho_n^\ast\le C
 \left(\frac{\log n_\ast}{n_\ast}\right)^{s/(2s+d)}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n_\ast\).  Under the strict-slack premise of \(\mathrm{thm:sharp\text{-}separation\text{-}lower}\), that established theorem supplies a constant \(c>0\) and a threshold beyond which
\[
 \rho_n^\ast\ge c
 \left(\frac{\log n_\ast}{n_\ast}\right)^{s/(2s+d)}.
\]
Taking the maximum of the upper- and lower-bound thresholds proves the displayed conditional matching frontier.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The class-uniform probability bound for the simultaneous raw-Hessian event at radius \(\mathfrak R_{H,n}\).
open_obligations.obstruction: Even after an affirmative resolution of \(\mathrm{oeq:global\text{-}endpoint\text{-}response}\), the frozen definitions of \(Q_{k_n}\) and \(K_{h_n}\) state neither the approximation and operator-envelope estimates nor the derivative and empirical-concentration estimates required to prove the asserted finite-sample probability bound. Those estimates are the statistical crux and cannot be inferred from a construction name or assumed as the event to be proved.
open_obligations.attempted: Extended the prior deterministic argument through clipping inactivity, inverse perturbation, eigenvalue and infimum stability, and exact size/power implications. Rechecked every bandwidth substitution and the negligibility of the second Bernstein and nonlinear-remainder terms. Also tested the presolve decomposition through the linearized kernel route; that route stops precisely at the unstated wavelet, smoothing-kernel, and concentration inequalities, while the presolve draft itself labels their bookkeeping incomplete.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The following deterministic and rate portions of the theorem do follow from the frozen core.  Suppose
\[
 \max_{a\in\mathcal A}\lVert\widetilde H_a-H_a\rVert_\infty
 \le r_{H,n}\le m/2.
 \tag{1}
\]
For every \(a\in\mathcal A\), \(u\in\Omega\), and unit vector \(x\), assumption \(\mathrm{ass:hessian\text{-}ellipticity}\) and (1) give
\[
 x^{\mathsf T}\widetilde H_a(u)x
 \ge x^{\mathsf T}H_a(u)x-r_{H,n}
 \ge m-r_{H,n}\ge m/2>m/4.
\]
Hence all eigenvalues of \(\widetilde H_a(u)\) exceed the clipping threshold in \(\Pi_{m/4}\), so Definition \(\mathrm{def:regularized\text{-}hessian\text{-}estimator}\) gives \(\widehat H_a=\widetilde H_a\) simultaneously.  In particular,
\[
 \lVert\widehat H_a-H_a\rVert_\infty\le r_{H,n},
 \qquad
 \lVert\widehat H_a^{-1}\rVert_\infty\le\frac2m,
 \qquad
 \lVert H_a^{-1}\rVert_\infty\le\frac1m,
 \qquad
 \lVert H_a\rVert_\infty\le M.
 \tag{2}
\]
For an ordered pair \(p\ne q\), add and subtract \(H_q\widehat H_p^{-1}\) and use
\(\widehat H_p^{-1}-H_p^{-1}=\widehat H_p^{-1}(H_p-\widehat H_p)H_p^{-1}\).  The submultiplicativity of the operator norm and (2) yield, uniformly in \(u\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \lVert\widehat H_q\widehat H_p^{-1}-H_qH_p^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 &\le
 \lVert\widehat H_q-H_q\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 \lVert\widehat H_p^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\\
 &\quad+
 \lVert H_q\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 \lVert\widehat H_p^{-1}(H_p-\widehat H_p)H_p^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\\
 &\le\left(\frac2m+\frac{2M}{m^2}\right)r_{H,n}=w_n.
\end{aligned}
 \tag{3}
\]
Since \(\lVert\operatorname{sym}(A)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le\lVert A\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\), the Rayleigh quotient implies
\[
 \left\lvert\lambda_{\min}(\widehat S_{pq}(u))
 -\lambda_{\min}(S_{pq}(u))\right\rvert\le w_n.
\]
Taking the supremum over \(u\), and using
\(\lvert\inf_u a(u)-\inf_u b(u)\rvert\le\sup_u\lvert a(u)-b(u)\rvert\), gives
\[
 \max_{p\ne q}\lvert\widehat\gamma_{pq}-\gamma_{pq}\rvert\le w_n.
 \tag{4}
\]
If \(\gamma_{pq}\le0\), equation (4) implies \(\widehat\gamma_{pq}\le w_n\), hence \(\Psi_n=0\).  If \(\gamma_{pq}\ge3w_n\), it implies \(\widehat\gamma_{pq}\ge2w_n>w_n\), hence \(\Psi_n=1\).  Therefore, whenever the event in (1) has probability at least \(1-\delta\), the test has type-I and type-II errors at most \(\delta\) on the null and separated alternative classes in the theorem.

It remains to verify the deterministic simplification of the displayed envelope.  From the definition of \(h_n\),
\[
 n_\ast h_n^{2s+d}=\ell_n,
\]
and therefore
\[
 \sqrt{\frac{\ell_n}{n_\ast h_n^d}}=h_n^s.
 \tag{5}
\]
Because \(k_n=h_n\ell_n^{-2/s}\), for fixed \(\delta\) one has \(\ell_n\asymp\log n_\ast\), \(\log(1/k_n)=O(\ell_n)\), and
\[
 k_n^s\{1+\log(1/k_n)\}
 =h_n^s\ell_n^{-2}\{1+\log(1/k_n)\}
 =O(h_n^s/\ell_n).
 \tag{6}
\]
The remaining linear term satisfies
\[
 \frac{\ell_n}{n_\ast(h_nk_n)^{d/2}}
 =h_n^{2s}\ell_n^{d/s}=o(h_n^s).
 \tag{7}
\]
Direct substitution into the definition of \(\eta_n\) gives
\[
 \eta_n
 =h_n^{s-r}\ell_n^{-2(s-r)/s}
 +h_n^{s-r}\ell_n^{(d+2r)/s}
 +h_n^{2s-r}\ell_n^{2(d+r)/s}.
 \tag{8}
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:smoothness\text{-}index}\), together with \(d\ge2\), gives \(s>4\).  Since \(r=(s+4)/4\), it follows that \(s-2r=(s-4)/2>0\).  Each squared summand in (8), divided by \(h_n^s\), is a positive power of \(h_n\) times a fixed power of \(\ell_n\), and hence tends to zero; the cross terms are bounded by sums of squares.  Thus
\[
 \eta_n^2=o(h_n^s).
 \tag{9}
\]
Equations (5)--(9) show that \(\mathfrak R_{H,n}\le C' h_n^s\) eventually for a class-dependent \(C'<\infty\).  Choosing \(C_1\ge C'\), and then increasing \(n_0\) because \(h_n^s\to0\), yields
\[
 \mathfrak R_{H,n}\le r_{H,n}=C_1h_n^s\le m/2.
\]
The only unproved part is the class-uniform stochastic assertion
\[
 \inf_{\mathbf P\in\mathcal M_s}
 \mathbb P_{\mathbf P}\!\left\{
 \max_{a\in\mathcal A}\lVert\widetilde H_a-H_a\rVert_\infty
 \le\mathfrak R_{H,n}\right\}\ge1-\delta.
\]
The affirmative endpoint-response conclusion would control the deterministic nonlinear response, but the frozen descriptions of \(Q_{k_n}\) and \(K_{h_n}\) do not supply the approximation, \(L^2\)-operator, kernel-envelope, derivative-envelope, or empirical concentration inequalities needed to derive this probability bound.  Treating that bound as an assumed event would assume the theorem's statistical crux.
